title: Powers of 10

blocks.html: You know that each place is ten times the place to its right: one, ten, hundred, thousand. Writing $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$ for ten thousand takes a while, so there is a short way: an exponent.
$10^{3}$ means $10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1{,}000$. The small raised number, the exponent, says how many 10s are multiplied. $10^{n}$ is a 1 followed by $n$ zeros.

Each time you multiply by 10, every digit moves one place to the left and a 0 fills the ones place. Start with 1 and multiply by 10 three times: $10$, then $100$, then $1{,}000$. Three factors of 10, three zeros.

blocks.cap: Press “× 10” again and again. Each press is one more factor of 10, and the 1 moves one place left.

blocks.title: A number times a power of ten

blocks.html: Reading $10^{3}$ as $10 \times 3 = 30$. The exponent is not a factor; it counts factors. Check: $10^{3}$ must be bigger than $10^{2} = 100$, and 30 is not.
